newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bosnian Serb leader says Karadzic arrest possible.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serb leader says Karadzic arrest possible.

text.p: Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic has said she would not shy away from arresting her nationalist hardline rivals led by indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic.
"The constitution gives me the right to deploy the army or the police -- as a last resort," Plavsic told the German magazine Der Spiegel in an interview to be published on Monday.
She said Karadzic, the former Bosnian Serb leader, and his supporters had been involved in corruption, helping dozens of companies dodge massive amounts of customs duty.
Asked why she did not simply arrest the culprits, she replied: "I will not be deterred from doing that if it is the last chance to save our people."

But she added such arrests would be difficult to carry out. "Even the interior minister (Dragan Kijac) whom I have dismissed belongs to those whom I call criminals," she said in the interview, which was released by Spiegel ahead of publication.

Plavsic said she could not extradite Karadzic to the U.N. War Crimes Tribunal at the Hague, where he has been indicted on charges of genocide, because it was not allowed under the Bosnian Serb constitution.
"He's also not guilty in the sense of the charges. He was a slave to his masters in Belgrade," she said.
Plavsic said U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright had offered not to pursue Karadzic if he agreed to leave Bosnia for good. But Karadzic had rejected the idea.

"He said: 'I founded the Republika Srpska and I want to continue to lead it.' Karadzic is at fault for everything," Plavsic told Spiegel. "He's behaving like a mother who gives birth to a child and then claims the right to kill it."
Plavsic is engaged in a bitter power struggle with Karadzic. She dissolved parliament and called fresh elections earlier this month to prevent his supporters ousting her from her post.
The Bosnian Serb constitutional court suspended the move a few days later while it considers whether Plavsic had acted within her power.
